passages.text: Better a poor man who walks with integrity than a fool whose lips are perverse.
passages.sermon:
A poor man can walk with integrity.
He lives honestly.
This is good.
A fool speaks with twisted words.
His lips are perverse.
It is better to be poor and honest than to be foolish and speak wrongly.
passages.original: טֽוֹב־ רָ֭שׁ הוֹלֵ֣ךְ בְּתֻמּ֑וֹ מֵעִקֵּ֥שׁ שְׂ֝פָתָ֗יו וְה֣וּא כְסִֽיל׃

passages.text: Even zeal is no good without knowledge, and he who hurries his footsteps misses the mark.
passages.sermon:
Zeal means strong enthusiasm.
Knowledge means understanding what is right.
Zeal without knowledge is not good.
A person who acts quickly without thinking makes mistakes.
Hurrying leads to sin.
passages.original: גַּ֤ם בְּלֹא־ דַ֣עַת נֶ֣פֶשׁ לֹא־ ט֑וֹב וְאָ֖ץ בְּרַגְלַ֣יִם חוֹטֵֽא׃

passages.text: A man’s own folly subverts his way, yet his heart rages against the LORD.
passages.sermon:
A man can act foolishly.
His own foolishness ruins his path.
He causes his own trouble.
He becomes angry at the LORD.
His heart blames God for his problems.
passages.original: אִוֶּ֣לֶת אָ֭דָם תְּסַלֵּ֣ף דַּרְכּ֑וֹ וְעַל־ יְ֝הוָ֗ה יִזְעַ֥ף לִבּֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Wealth attracts many friends, but a poor man is deserted by his friend.
passages.sermon:
Wealth brings many friends.
A rich person gains many companions.
A poor person loses his friend.
A poor man is left alone by his companion.
passages.original: ה֗וֹן יֹ֭סִיף רֵעִ֣ים רַבִּ֑ים וְ֝דָ֗ל מֵרֵ֥עהוּ יִפָּרֵֽד׃

passages.text: A false witness will not go unpunished, and one who utters lies will not escape.
passages.sermon:
A false witness speaks lies about others.
God will punish a false witness.
A person who tells lies will not escape punishment.
God will not let liars go free.
passages.original: עֵ֣ד שְׁ֭קָרִים לֹ֣א יִנָּקֶ֑ה וְיָפִ֥יחַ כְּ֝זָבִ֗ים לֹ֣א יִמָּלֵֽט׃

passages.text: Many seek the favor of the prince, and everyone is a friend of the gift giver.
passages.sermon:
A prince is a person with power and wealth.
Many people try to please the prince.
A gift giver is someone who gives gifts to others.
Everyone wants to be friends with the gift giver.
passages.original: רַ֭בִּים יְחַלּ֣וּ פְנֵֽי־ נָדִ֑יב וְכָל־ הָ֝רֵ֗עַ לְאִ֣ישׁ מַתָּֽן׃

passages.text: All the brothers of a poor man hate him— how much more do his friends avoid him! He may pursue them with pleading, but they are nowhere to be found.
passages.sermon:
A poor man has brothers.
His brothers hate him.
His friends avoid him even more.
He chases after them with words.
They are not there.
He cannot find them.
passages.original: כָּ֥ל אֲחֵי־ רָ֨שׁ׀ שְֽׂנֵאֻ֗הוּ אַ֤ף כִּ֣י מְ֭רֵעֵהוּ רָחֲק֣וּ מִמֶּ֑נּוּ מְרַדֵּ֖ף אֲמָרִ֣ים לֹא הֵֽמָּה׃

passages.text: He who acquires wisdom loves himself; one who safeguards understanding will find success.
passages.sermon:
A wise person loves himself.
A wise person seeks wisdom.
A person who keeps understanding will find good things.
A person who guards understanding will succeed.
passages.original: קֹֽנֶה־ לֵּ֭ב אֹהֵ֣ב נַפְשׁ֑וֹ שֹׁמֵ֥ר תְּ֝בוּנָ֗ה לִמְצֹא־ טֽוֹב׃

passages.text: A false witness will not go unpunished, and one who pours out lies will perish.
passages.sermon: A false witness will not escape punishment.\r\nA person who tells lies will be destroyed.
passages.original: עֵ֣ד שְׁ֭קָרִים לֹ֣א יִנָּקֶ֑ה וְיָפִ֖יחַ כְּזָבִ֣ים יֹאבֵֽד׃פ

passages.text: Luxury is unseemly for a fool— how much worse for a slave to rule over princes!
passages.sermon:
A fool does not deserve luxury.
Luxury does not fit a fool.
A slave should not rule over princes.
It is even worse when a slave rules over princes.
A fool and a slave both lack the qualities needed for honor and leadership.
Luxury and authority belong to those with wisdom and noble character.
passages.original: לֹֽא־ נָאוֶ֣ה לִכְסִ֣יל תַּעֲנ֑וּג אַ֝֗ף כִּֽי־ לְעֶ֤בֶד׀ מְשֹׁ֬ל בְּשָׂרִֽים׃

passages.text: A man’s insight gives him patience, and his virtue is to overlook an offense.
passages.sermon:
A wise person shows patience.
Insight helps a person wait calmly.
It is good to overlook an offense.
Forgiving others is a sign of virtue.
passages.original: שֵׂ֣כֶל אָ֭דָם הֶאֱרִ֣יךְ אַפּ֑וֹ וְ֝תִפאַרְתּ֗וֹ עֲבֹ֣ר עַל־ פָּֽשַׁע׃

passages.text: A king’s rage is like the roar of a lion, but his favor is like dew on the grass.
passages.sermon:
A king is a ruler with great power.
A king’s anger is very strong.
A king’s anger is loud and frightening.
A king’s anger is like a lion’s roar.
A king’s favor is gentle.
A king’s favor brings blessing.
A king’s favor is like dew on the grass.
passages.original: נַ֣הַם כַּ֭כְּפִיר זַ֣עַף מֶ֑לֶךְ וּכְטַ֖ל עַל־ עֵ֣שֶׂב רְצוֹנֽוֹ׃

passages.text: A foolish son is his father’s ruin, and a quarrelsome wife is like a constant dripping.
passages.sermon: A foolish son brings ruin to his father.\r\nA quarrelsome wife causes constant trouble.\r\nHer arguments are like water that drips without stopping.
passages.original: הַוֺּ֣ת לְ֭אָבִיו בֵּ֣ן כְּסִ֑יל וְדֶ֥לֶף טֹ֝רֵ֗ד מִדְיְנֵ֥י אִשָּֽׁה׃

passages.text: Houses and wealth are inherited from fathers, but a prudent wife is from the LORD.
passages.sermon:
Fathers give houses to their children.
Fathers give wealth to their children.
The LORD gives a prudent wife.
A prudent wife comes from the LORD.
passages.original: בַּ֣יִת וָ֭הוֹן נַחֲלַ֣ת אָב֑וֹת וּ֝מֵיְהוָ֗ה אִשָּׁ֥ה מַשְׂכָּֽלֶת׃

passages.text: Laziness brings on deep sleep, and an idle soul will suffer hunger.
passages.sermon:
Laziness causes deep sleep.
A lazy person will become very tired.
An idle soul will go hungry.
A person who does not work will not have enough food.
passages.original: עַ֭צְלָה תַּפִּ֣יל תַּרְדֵּמָ֑ה וְנֶ֖פֶשׁ רְמִיָּ֣ה תִרְעָֽב׃

passages.text: He who keeps a commandment preserves his soul, but he who is careless in his ways will die.
passages.sermon: A person who keeps God's commandments protects his own life.\r\nA person who ignores his ways will die.
passages.original: שֹׁמֵ֣ר מִ֭צְוָה שֹׁמֵ֣ר נַפְשׁ֑וֹ בּוֹזֵ֖ה דְרָכָ֣יו יוּמָת׃

passages.text: Kindness to the poor is a loan to the LORD, and He will repay the lender.
passages.sermon:
The LORD is God.
The LORD values kindness.
A person who helps the poor shows kindness.
When a person helps the poor, it is like lending to the LORD.
The LORD will repay the person who helps the poor.
passages.original: מַלְוֵ֣ה יְ֭הוָה ח֣וֹנֵֽן דָּ֑ל וּ֝גְמֻל֗וֹ יְשַׁלֶּם־ לֽוֹ׃

passages.text: Discipline your son, for in that there is hope; do not be party to his death.
passages.sermon:
A father must discipline his son.
Discipline gives hope for the son.
Do not desire your son’s death.
Do not support actions that lead to his destruction.
passages.original: יַסֵּ֣ר בִּ֭נְךָ כִּי־ יֵ֣שׁ תִּקְוָ֑ה וְאֶל־ הֲ֝מִית֗וֹ אַל־ תִּשָּׂ֥א נַפְשֶֽׁךָ׃

passages.text: A man of great anger must pay the penalty; if you rescue him, you will have to do so again.
passages.sermon:
A man with great anger must face punishment.
He must pay for his actions.
If you rescue this angry man from the consequences,
You will need to rescue him again.
He will repeat his offense.
Your help will not change him.
passages.original: גֹּרַל חֵ֭מָה נֹ֣שֵׂא עֹ֑נֶשׁ כִּ֥י אִם־ תַּ֝צִּ֗יל וְע֣וֹד תּוֹסִֽף׃

passages.text: Listen to counsel and accept discipline, that you may be wise the rest of your days.
passages.sermon:
You must listen to advice.
You must accept correction.
If you do this, you will become wise.
You will remain wise for the rest of your life.
passages.original: שְׁמַ֣ע עֵ֭צָה וְקַבֵּ֣ל מוּסָ֑ר לְ֝מַ֗עַן תֶּחְכַּ֥ם בְּאַחֲרִיתֶֽךָ׃

passages.text: Many plans are in a man’s heart, but the purpose of the LORD will prevail.
passages.sermon:
A man often has many plans in his heart.
He thinks about many things he wants to do.
But the LORD has His own purpose.
The LORD’s purpose will stand.
The LORD’s plan will succeed.
passages.original: רַבּ֣וֹת מַחֲשָׁב֣וֹת בְּלֶב־ אִ֑ישׁ וַעֲצַ֥ת יְ֝הוָ֗ה הִ֣יא תָקֽוּם׃

passages.text: The desire of a man is loving devotion; better to be poor than a liar.
passages.sermon:
A man desires loving devotion.
Loving devotion means kindness and faithfulness.
It is better to be poor than to be a liar.
A poor person is honest.
A liar is not trustworthy.
Honesty is better than wealth gained by lies.
passages.original: תַּאֲוַ֣ת אָדָ֣ם חַסְדּ֑וֹ וְטֽוֹב־ רָ֝שׁ מֵאִ֥ישׁ כָּזָֽב׃

passages.text: The fear of the LORD leads to life, that one may rest content, without visitation from harm.
passages.sermon:
The fear of the LORD leads to life.
A person who fears the LORD will live.
This person will rest with satisfaction.
No harm will visit this person.
passages.original: יִרְאַ֣ת יְהוָ֣ה לְחַיִּ֑ים וְשָׂבֵ֥עַ יָ֝לִ֗ין בַּל־ יִפָּ֥קֶד רָֽע׃

passages.text: The slacker buries his hand in the dish; he will not even bring it back to his mouth.
passages.sermon:
A slacker is a lazy person.
A slacker puts his hand in the dish.
He does not bring his hand back to his mouth.
He does not eat the food.
He does not finish what he starts.
passages.original: טָ֘מַ֤ן עָצֵ֣ל יָ֭דוֹ בַּצַּלָּ֑חַת גַּם־ אֶל־ פִּ֝֗יהוּ לֹ֣א יְשִׁיבֶֽנָּה׃

passages.text: Strike a mocker, and the simple will beware; rebuke the discerning man, and he will gain knowledge.
passages.sermon:
A mocker is a person who scorns or ridicules others.
Strike the mocker.
The simple person will see this.
The simple person will become cautious.
A discerning man is someone who understands and thinks deeply.
Rebuke the discerning man.
He will gain knowledge.
passages.original: לֵ֣ץ תַּ֭כֶּה וּפֶ֣תִי יַעְרִ֑ם וְהוֹכִ֥יחַ לְ֝נָב֗וֹן יָבִ֥ין דָּֽעַת׃

passages.text: He who assaults his father or evicts his mother is a son who brings shame and disgrace.
passages.sermon:
A son may attack his father.
A son may drive his mother away.
This son brings shame.
This son brings disgrace.
passages.original: מְֽשַׁדֶּד־ אָ֭ב יַבְרִ֣יחַ אֵ֑ם בֵּ֝֗ן מֵבִ֥ישׁ וּמַחְפִּֽיר׃

passages.text: If you cease to hear instruction, my son, you will stray from the words of knowledge.
passages.sermon:
A father speaks to his son.
He gives a warning.
He says, “My son, do not stop listening to instruction.”
If you stop listening to instruction, you will go astray.
You will wander from the words of knowledge.
passages.original: חַֽדַל־ בְּ֭נִי לִשְׁמֹ֣עַ מוּסָ֑ר לִ֝שְׁג֗וֹת מֵֽאִמְרֵי־ דָֽעַת׃

passages.text: A corrupt witness mocks justice, and a wicked mouth swallows iniquity.
passages.sermon:
A corrupt witness mocks justice.
A wicked person speaks evil.
A wicked mouth accepts wrongdoing.
A wicked mouth covers up sin.
passages.original: עֵ֣ד בְּ֭לִיַּעַל יָלִ֣יץ מִשְׁפָּ֑ט וּפִ֥י רְ֝שָׁעִ֗ים יְבַלַּע־ אָֽוֶן׃

passages.text: Judgments are prepared for mockers, and beatings for the backs of fools.
passages.sermon:
God prepares judgments for mockers.
God prepares beatings for the backs of fools.
Mockers receive judgment.
Fools receive punishment.
passages.original: נָכ֣וֹנוּ לַלֵּצִ֣ים שְׁפָטִ֑ים וּ֝מַהֲלֻמ֗וֹת לְגֵ֣ו כְּסִילִֽים׃
